taxonomy_source: Brown & Altadmri (2017) novice misconceptions A-R + 2025 SLR; Python-focused subset

M-02.name: off_by_one_range
M-02.desc: Believes range(a,b) includes b; loop boundary confusion
M-02.example: for i in range(1,10): expects 10 included

M-03.name: mutable_aliasing
M-03.desc: Thinks b = a copies a list; mutation surprises

M-05.name: type_confusion_str_num
M-05.desc: Mixes strings and numbers in operations

M-06.name: loop_condition_never_updates
M-06.desc: Loop variable not updated -> infinite loop concept gap

M-07.name: indentation_block_scope
M-07.desc: Does not understand which lines belong to if/for block
M-07.example: second line unindented but meant inside loop

M-08.name: print_vs_return
M-08.desc: Confuses printing with returning; expects print to give usable value
M-08.example: y = print(x) then uses y in math

M-09.name: SLOPPINESS_NEGATIVE_CLASS
M-09.desc: NOT a misconception: typo/habit slip with correct concept. Same surface error, different treatment.
M-09.example: x == 5 likhna tha, jaldi me x = 5 ho gaya (student knows the rule)

golden_rule: M-09 is the differentiator: model must NOT treat every error as a conceptual gap. Use error + code pattern + chat signal to separate.
